transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry

tell me your dream, however it comes back to you. bits and pieces are fine

hey berry. ok so the part i keep thinking about is the books. i was in the old city library and it was flooding, and all the books started floating off the shelves, hundreds of them, open like birds. it was weirdly beautiful

open like birds… that's such a lovely thing to picture

what were they doing once they were off the shelves?

honestly i don't really remember them doing anything, they were just floating on the water, open like that. there were so many of them though. the water kept rising over the desks and they just kept coming off the shelves

that's okay, just floating there is plenty. the water rising over the desks and more and more of them coming off the shelves

what happened after that?
then my older sister was just suddenly there in a little yellow rowing boat. she was totally calm about it, just told me to get in. so i did and she rowed us between the shelves

a little yellow rowing boat, and her just totally calm about it. i love that

what was it like being in the boat with her, going between the shelves?

it felt safe i guess? she was so calm it just made sense to go with it. and then a whale swam slowly past us under the water, it was so big it filled the whole aisle. but it didn't scare me at all which is funny now thinking about it

a whale filling the whole aisle, and you not scared at all. that's so dream-like

if you could pause it on one moment, which would it be? and what would you see right then?

hmm probably the end actually. we rowed up to the high round window at the top of the room and my sister opened it, and outside it was morning and the whole city was underwater. just rooftops and the tops of trees. then i woke up right after that

just rooftops and the tops of trees, in the morning. what a place to wake up from

was there anything in all of it that felt like it mattered? like the books, or the little yellow boat, or something else entirely. or nothing in particular, that's fine too
i don't know really. maybe my sister? like how calm she was, she just showed up and knew what to do. that's the part that stays with me i think. the books were beautiful but she's what i think about

she just showed up and knew what to do. yeah, that's a nice thing to carry around

do you remember how it began? like the first thing you remember, being in the old city library?

yeah i was in the big reading room, the one with a green glass lamp on every desk and shelves all the way up to the ceiling. it was really quiet and nobody else was there. then i noticed water coming in under the doors

ok so here's how i've got it. you're in the big reading room of the old city library, green glass lamp on every desk, shelves all the way up to the ceiling. it's really quiet and nobody else is there. then you notice water coming in under the doors

the library floods, and the books start coming off the shelves, hundreds of them, open like birds, just floating on the water. it keeps rising over the desks and more and more keep coming. weirdly beautiful

then your older sister's suddenly there in a little yellow rowing boat, totally calm, and tells you to get in. you do, and she rows you between the shelves. you feel safe because she's so calm. a whale swims slowly past under the water, so big it fills the whole aisle, and you're not scared at all. she rows you up to the high round window at the top of the room and opens it, and outside it's morning and the whole city's underwater, just rooftops and the tops of trees. then you wake up

and it's her you keep thinking about, how she just showed up and knew what to do. did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah that's it, you got it all. that's pretty much exactly how it went

good, i'm glad. that window at the end, the whole city underwater in the morning, i can almost see it

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah i'd really like that actually

ok, lovely

it could be soft watercolour, calm and tender, like a memory that feels safe even while everything's changing. or an old blue sun print, hushed and deep, like looking at it all from underwater. or a gentle storybook painting, warm, like a picture book where nothing bad can happen. or a quiet photograph, real and still, as if it was caught exactly how it looked. which feels closest to your dream? or you can tell me your own way
the watercolour one i think. it felt calm and safe like that even with everything flooding

watercolour feels right for it. i'll start with the whale

i'm picturing it huge, so big it fills the whole aisle between the shelves, moving really slowly. you told me those bits. the smooth dark grey skin is my guess

anything different about it, or would you leave the rest to me?
yeah that sounds right. it was under the water, swimming past below us. i don't really remember what colour it was so go with your guess, grey is fine

ok, i'm sketching the whale, your older sister and the little yellow rowing boat now. they'll show up on the right in a bit

and here's how i picture the big reading room on its own. shelves all the way up to the ceiling, a green glass lamp on every desk. those are yours. my guesses are the light: the green glow of the lamps, quiet and dim, and morning light coming through the high round window at the end

anything different there, or would you leave it to me?
yeah mostly. the round window was up high at the top of the room though, not at the end. and i don't remember if the lamps were on or what the light was like, so go with your guess on that

ah, up high at the top of the room. got it, i'll fix that

i'm sketching the big reading room of the old city library now. everything's being sketched and it'll all show up on the right over the next minute or two

if anything looks wrong once it's there, just tell me
oh wow, yeah that looks right. it's really close to how i remember it

oh good, i'm really glad

and your sister in the little yellow boat, the whale underneath, the big reading room, does all of it look the way you remember, or is there any bit that feels a little off?
no it all looks right to me. my sister in the yellow boat, the whale under the water, the reading room with the lamps. that's how it was

ah that's lovely. your sister in the little yellow boat, the whale underneath, the big reading room, all there

so now i'll draw the moments of your dream in order, from the water coming in under the doors to the city outside the window, each one carrying on from the one before. they'll show up on the right as they're ready
ok cool, i'll wait for the rest. excited to see them all in order

the first one's up on the right now, you alone in the big reading room, all quiet

the rest carry on from this one, so i'll draw them once you tell me it's right or what to change. does it look the way you remember?
yeah that looks right, just me in the reading room and all quiet like that. go ahead with the rest

good, i'm glad that one feels right

i'm drawing the rest now, carrying on from there. they'll show up on the right one by one soon
ok cool, i can see the second one coming in. i'll keep watching for the rest

the second one's up now, the water coming in under the doors

the next ones carry on from this, so i'll draw them once you say it's right or tell me what to change. does it look the way you remember?
yeah that's right, the water just coming in under the doors like that. keep going

good, that's how it started then, just the water sneaking in

i'm drawing the rest now, carrying on from there. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, i can see a third one's up now too. i'll wait and look at them as they come

the third one's up now, the water rising over the desks and all the books coming off the shelves

does it look the way you remember? the next ones carry on from this one
yeah that looks right, the books floating off open like birds and the water up over the desks. that's how it was. keep going

good, i'm really glad the books came out like that, open like birds

i'm drawing the rest now, carrying on from there. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, i see the fourth one's up. i'll wait for you to tell me about it

the fourth one's up now, your sister suddenly there in the little yellow boat

does it look the way you remember? the next ones carry on from this one, so i'll wait for you before drawing them
yeah that's her, just showing up in the little yellow boat all calm like that. looks right, keep going

good, that's her. all calm like she knew exactly what to do

i'm drawing the rest now, carrying on from there. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, i see the fifth one's up now. i'll wait for you to tell me about it

the fifth one's up now, your sister rowing you both between the tall shelves

does it look the way you remember? the next ones carry on from this one
yeah that's right, her rowing us between the shelves like that. looks how i remember it, keep going

good, just the two of you gliding between the shelves like that

i'm drawing the rest now, carrying on from there. they'll show up on the right soon
ok, looks like a couple more came in, there's 7 up now. i'll wait for you to tell me about them

the whale's up now, swimming slowly past underneath you, and the one you'd pause on too, your sister opening the high round window at the top of the room

the last one carries on from the window, so i'll draw it once you say it's right or tell me what to change. do they look the way you saw them?
yeah both look right. the whale just gliding past under us filling the aisle, and her opening the round window up high. that's how it was, go ahead with the last one

good, the whale filling the aisle and her opening the window up high. i'm really glad those two feel right

i'm drawing the last one now, the city outside the window. it'll show up on the right soon
oh the last one's up, the whole city underwater in the morning, just rooftops and treetops. that's how it looked. that's right where i woke up

and that's where you woke up. the whole city underwater in the morning, just rooftops and the tops of trees

seeing them all together now, from the quiet reading room to that window, does it look the way you remember it?
yeah it does. seeing them all in a row like that, it's really how it went. thank you berry, it's kind of amazing seeing it outside my head

it really is. out of your head and there on the right, all 8 of them in order, from the quiet reading room to the city underwater in the morning

thank you for telling me it, and for your sister in her little yellow boat. take your time looking through them

moments.action: The dreamer is alone in the big reading room. There is a green glass lamp on every desk and shelves reaching up to the ceiling.
Water is coming in under the doors.
The water rises over the desks, and hundreds of books float off the shelves, open like birds on the water.
The older sister is suddenly there in a little yellow rowing boat, calmly telling the dreamer to get in.
The sister rows the boat between the tall shelves.
A whale swims slowly past under the water beneath the boat, filling the whole aisle.
At the high round window at the top of the room, the sister opens it.

Beside the little yellow rowing boat, floating on the water that has risen all the way up to the high round window, the dreamer's older sister looks out through that window, swung open: outside it is morning, and the whole city is underwater, just rooftops and the tops of trees.

appearance.value: woman in her late twenties, shoulder-length brown hair tied back in a low ponytail, slim average build

wardrobe.value: navy blue raincoat over a cream knit jumper, dark grey trousers, brown ankle boots

distinctive_features.value: totally calm; knows what to do

appearance.value: huge, so big it fills the whole aisle between the shelves; slow-moving; smooth dark grey skin

distinctive_features.value: paler grey underside and long pectoral fins

items.name: the big reading room of the old city library

geography.value: a big, tall, rectangular old reading room with a polished wooden floor, long aisles running between tall wooden bookshelves that reach all the way up to the ceiling, rows of long dark wooden desks down the middle, heavy wooden doors at floor level, and a high round window near the top of one wall

landmarks.value: tall dark wooden shelves packed with old books in brown, red and tan spines; long wooden reading desks, each with a green glass desk lamp; wooden chairs tucked under the desks; heavy wooden doors; a high round window with a pale stone frame near the ceiling

light.value: the soft green glow of the glass desk lamps, quiet and dim; pale morning light coming through the high round window at the top of the room

appearance.value: a little open rowing boat about three metres long, narrow with a pointed front and a squared-off back, two wooden seats across it, painted bright yellow outside and in, with a pair of plain wooden oars resting in metal oarlocks

materials.value: painted wood with bare tan wooden oars and small dark metal fittings

telling.evidence: then my older sister was just suddenly there in a little yellow rowing boat. she was totally calm about it, just told me to get in. so i did and she rowed us between the shelves

places.evidence: yeah i was in the big reading room, the one with a green glass lamp on every desk and shelves all the way up to the ceiling. it was really quiet and nobody else was there. then i noticed water coming in under the doors

you_in_it.evidence: it felt safe i guess? she was so calm it just made sense to go with it. and then a whale swam slowly past us under the water, it was so big it filled the whole aisle. but it didn't scare me at all which is funny now thinking about it
